reason: AFG is a risk-bearing specialty P&C insurance carrier. It underwrites policies and earns premiums plus investment income. It sells through independent agents and brokers (T:P2.2, T:P2.3). The Baldwin Group is an insurance distributor and advisory firm. It places coverage with carriers and earns commissions and fees. It also serves individuals and families, and sells benefits and wealth management (C:P1.2, C:P1.4). The two share an insurance label and some commercial customers. But they are in different parts of the value chain, with different economics: AFG carries underwriting risk, while Baldwin is a broker that is largely a customer channel for carriers like AFG.
reason_if_0: Different business model: carrier that underwrites risk and earns premiums versus broker/advisor that earns commissions and fees. Baldwin also has a large personal lines, benefits and wealth component that AFG lacks.
